page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor featuring the x86_64 architecture. The server delivers 12 vCPUs derived from 6 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem provides 48.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and BMI2 bit manipulation extensions, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache.

This server instance operates without bundled local storage and includes no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity is configured with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent disk storage and external networking must be integrated separately via external block storage and elastic IP configurations.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,870.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11,955.1, placing it firmly in the middle 50% band. Stress-ng multi-core testing reached 10,489.01 points, accompanied by 10.32 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.06 GB per second in static web serving throughput. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 71.48 GB per second, and write throughput reached 43.18 GB per second. In contrast, single-core execution reflects lower efficiency, as shown by weak relative ratings in single-core stress-ng tests (1,311.98) and single-threaded gzip compression (22.79 GB per second).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, ecs.g6.3xlarge provides solid value for multi-threaded applications that can saturate its 12 vCPUs while utilizing balanced memory. However, workloads requiring high single-thread clock execution or fast integrated scratch storage will encounter throughput limitations. The instance is suited for multi-tier enterprise web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservice orchestration clusters, background batch processing, and medium-scale database hosting.

Configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external block volumes and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal middle-tier multi-threaded capability, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 11,955.1, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 5,870.0, and 10.32 million Redis SET operations per second.
